chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليهما السلام, who said:

When you have dried the deceased, proceed to the camphor and wipe with it the traces of sajdah and all of his joints. Put some of the ḥanūṭ in his mouth, ears, head, and beard, and upon his chest and private part. And he said: The ḥanūṭ of the man and the woman is the same.

key_terms.آثَارَ السُّجُودِ: the marks or places of prostration on the body
key_terms.الْحَنُوطِ: the perfuming substance placed on the deceased
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person being prepared for burial

ai.seo_question: How should ḥanūṭ and camphor be applied to the deceased in Shia funeral rites?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on applying camphor and ḥanūṭ to the deceased during funerary preparation. It specifies the bodily areas where it is to be applied and states that the ḥanūṭ ruling is the same for both men and women.
